**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 20, 2026
**Re:** Vougeir Linen Services, Inc.: Review of TruRoute Linen Suite License Documents with Trutour Systems, LLC

---

## 1. Executive Summary

Vougeir licenses the **TruRoute Linen Suite**, Trutour's hosted RFID linen tracking and route management platform. The license is under a Software License Agreement with an **Effective Date of March 1, 2025** (the "License Agreement"). Key terms:

- **Initial Term:** three years (§12.1), then automatic one-year renewals (§12.2).
- **Annual License Fee:** $486,000 (§4.1).
- **Governing law and forum:** Delaware law, Wilmington, Delaware courts (§18.1).

I reviewed all seven documents in the folder:

- the License Agreement;
- the Quality Agreement;
- the January 17, 2025 term sheet;
- Vougeir's September 14, 2026 fee objection letter;
- Trutour's October 6, 2026 side letter adding plants and seats;
- Trutour's draft v2 of the license (February 11, 2025); and
- the May 19, 2025 go-live confirmation email.

I found **four issues**. In order of priority:

| # | Priority | Issue | Location | Deadline / Trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Critical (most urgent)** | Trutour's consent is needed for the Ostrander acquisition. The side letter expressly does not give it. | License Agreement §14.3 (with §§14.2, 1.1(c), 13.4); Side Letter Recital B and §4.2 | Must be resolved before the expected January 2027 closing |
| 2 | **High** | Vougeir's fee-increase objection was late, so Trutour can treat the increase as deemed accepted. | License Agreement §4.4; Vougeir letter of Sept. 14, 2026, ¶1 | Increase to $559,000 takes effect March 1, 2027 |
| 3 | **High** | Trutour may assign the license to anyone, including a Vougeir competitor, without Vougeir's consent. | License Agreement §14.1 (cf. §14.2; Term Sheet §11.1) | Ongoing exposure; best leverage is now |
| 4 | **Medium** | Service-credit disputes fall under New York law and forum, while all other claims stay in Delaware. | Quality Agreement §9.1; License Agreement §1.3 | Next outage dispute |

Issues 1 and 2 should be raised with Trutour together. Trutour has full discretion over the change-of-control consent, and the fee dispute will almost certainly become part of the price of that consent. Issues 3 and 4 should be put into the same amendment package.

---

## 2. Issues, Analysis and Recommendations

### Issue 1: Ostrander acquisition requires Trutour's consent, which has not been obtained (CRITICAL)

**Where:**
- License Agreement §14.3, read with §1.1(c) (definition of "Change of Control"), §14.2 and §13.4.
- Side Letter dated October 6, 2026, Recital B and §4.2.

**What the documents say:**
- **License Agreement §14.3.** A "Change of Control of Licensee is deemed an assignment of this Agreement by Licensee for purposes of Section 14.2." Trutour "may grant or withhold its consent to a Change of Control of Licensee in its **sole discretion**." If a Change of Control occurs without Trutour's prior written consent, Trutour may terminate on **30 days' written notice**.
- **License Agreement §1.1(c).** "Change of Control" includes a merger after which Vougeir's pre-transaction equity holders hold less than 50% of the survivor. It also includes any acquisition of more than 50% of Vougeir's voting equity.
- **Side Letter Recital B.** The side letter recites "the proposed acquisition of Licensee by Ostrander Linen Group, Inc." under a merger agreement signed September 28, 2026, with closing expected in January 2027.
- **Side Letter §4.2.** It then states that "**[n]othing herein constitutes a consent or waiver under the Agreement**" and that it does not limit any right or remedy of either Party.

**Why it matters to Vougeir:**
- An acquisition of Vougeir by Ostrander is almost certainly a Change of Control under §1.1(c)(i) or (ii). It therefore triggers §14.3.
- The side letter may look as if Trutour has accommodated the deal, since it adds the Bethlehem and Cherry Hill plants and raises the seat count to 210 "in anticipation of the combined business after closing." It has not. §4.2 is an express non-consent and non-waiver clause. **Trutour's consent has not been obtained.**
- If the deal closes without written consent, Trutour can terminate on 30 days' notice. Under §13.4 Vougeir would then **lose its refund of prepaid fees**, because §13.4 excludes refunds where Licensor terminates under §14.3. That would include the Annual License Fee and the side-letter plant and seat fees invoiced in advance.
- The TruRoute platform runs Vougeir's RFID scanning, inventory reconciliation and daily route dispatch. Quality Agreement Recital B and §1.1(b) list these as Core Functions. Losing the platform on 30 days' notice right after closing would be operationally severe.
- Because consent is in Trutour's sole discretion, Trutour has substantial leverage. It may try to condition consent on accepting the $559,000 fee (see Issue 2) or on other concessions.
- The missing consent is also likely a disclosure or closing-condition item under the Ostrander merger agreement. We have not seen that agreement.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Promptly request Trutour's prior written consent** to the Ostrander Change of Control under §14.3. Ask that it be documented as a signed instrument that complies with §18.3. Target signature well before the January 2027 closing.
2. In the same instrument, seek an amendment to §14.3 that:
   - replaces "sole discretion" with "not unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed"; and
   - permits a Change of Control to a non-competitor of Trutour without consent, or on notice only.
3. Seek a §13.4 amendment so that a §14.3 termination does not forfeit prepaid fees.
4. Coordinate with Ostrander's deal counsel. Confirm how this contract is treated in the merger agreement's consent schedule and closing conditions. Advise the client **not to close** without the consent in hand, or without an express waiver of Trutour's §14.3 termination right.
5. As context for negotiation, note that Trutour's own draft v2 (§§14.1–14.2) treated a Change of Control as an assignment requiring the other Party's consent. That draft included no "sole discretion" language and no specific termination right. The final §14.3 is more Trutour-favorable than the draft the parties had been negotiating.

---

### Issue 2: Fee-increase objection was sent after the 30-day window closed (HIGH)

**Where:**
- License Agreement §4.4.
- Vougeir letter to Trutour dated September 14, 2026, ¶1.

**What the documents say:**
- **License Agreement §4.4.**
  - Trutour may raise the Annual License Fee, effective on an anniversary of the Effective Date, on at least 90 days' notice.
  - Vougeir may object "within thirty (30) days after the date of Licensor's fee adjustment notice." If Vougeir does not object within that period, "the adjusted fee is **deemed accepted by Licensee**."
  - If Vougeir objects in time, the parties negotiate, and the old fee continues for the following contract year if they cannot agree.
- **Vougeir letter ¶1.** The letter refers to Trutour's notice **dated August 3, 2026**, which raises the fee from $486,000 to **$559,000** (about 15%) effective **March 1, 2027**. It states, "We do not accept the proposed increase." The letter is dated **September 14, 2026**.

**Why it matters to Vougeir:**
- Thirty days after August 3, 2026 is **September 2, 2026**. Vougeir's objection was sent **12 days late**.
- Trutour's notice itself appears timely. It was given more than 90 days before the March 1, 2027 anniversary.
- On the face of §4.4, Trutour can treat the $559,000 fee as deemed accepted. That is **$73,000 more per year**, on top of the new side-letter plant and seat fees.
- The letter's assumption that the old fee "continues" pending negotiation (¶4) applies only to a *timely* objection. Vougeir's reservation of rights in ¶5 does not cure the lateness.
- Vougeir cannot avoid the increase by non-renewal. The three-year Initial Term runs through February 2028, so the March 1, 2027–February 29, 2028 contract year is locked in.
- Nothing in the folder shows that Trutour has responded, waived the deadline, or invoiced the higher fee. Nothing shows that Vougeir has paid or agreed to it.
- Draft v2 §4.4 had no deemed-acceptance language. Comparing the drafts helps commercially but does not change the signed text.

**Recommended fix:**
1. Do not treat the September 14 letter as a timely objection in any further correspondence. Avoid statements that would harden the record.
2. **Seek Trutour's written waiver** of the §4.4 deadline, or a negotiated fee, before March 1, 2027. The practical lever is the change-of-control consent in Issue 1: package the fee and the consent in one negotiation and one signed amendment.
3. Confirm with the client whether anyone at Vougeir communicated an objection to Trutour on or before September 2, 2026 (email, call notes, meeting minutes). Also confirm the actual date the August 3 notice was delivered under §16.1. If an earlier written objection exists, it may preserve the §4.4 mechanism. If no such facts exist, we should not count on any argument.
4. Going forward, diarize the §4.4 objection window and the §12.2 non-renewal deadline (90 days before each term end). Add these to the client's contract-management calendar.

---

### Issue 3: Trutour may assign the license to anyone, including a Vougeir competitor (HIGH)

**Where:**
- License Agreement §14.1, contrasted with §14.2.
- Term Sheet §11.1.

**What the documents say:**
- **License Agreement §14.1.** Trutour "may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any Affiliate or **to any third party without Licensee's consent**." It need only give notice within 30 days *after* the assignment takes effect.
- **License Agreement §14.2.** Vougeir, by contrast, may not assign without Trutour's prior written consent.
- **Term Sheet §11.1.** The January 17, 2025 term sheet provided that "**[n]either party may assign without the other party's prior written consent**." Draft v2 §14.1 also had a mutual consent requirement.

**Why it matters to Vougeir:**
- The hosted platform holds Vougeir's "Licensee Data" (§1.1(e)). That includes customer lists, delivery routes, route schedules, pricing, linen inventory and linen-volume data, which are Vougeir's most competitively sensitive information.
- Under §14.1, Trutour could transfer the agreement, and with it hosting of that data, to a competing laundry or linen-rental operator or its affiliate. Vougeir would have no say and would learn of it only after the fact.
- The confidentiality protections (§§5 and 6) would bind the assignee only as a successor (§14.4). They do not prevent the competitor from owning the system that holds Vougeir's data.
- A partial assignment ("in whole or in part") could also split support, hosting and service-level accountability across entities.
- The final text departs from the agreed mutual restriction in the term sheet. The term sheet is non-binding (§1.2), so this is a negotiating point, not a breach claim. It is still a strong one.

**Recommended fix:**
1. Amend §14.1 to restore the term-sheet position: Trutour may not assign without Vougeir's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
2. At a minimum, Vougeir's consent should be required for any assignment to a competitor of Vougeir or its affiliates, or to any entity providing commercial laundry or linen-rental services. Any permitted assignment should also be subject to the following:
   - the assignee assumes all obligations in writing, including the Quality Agreement;
   - the assignee is expressly bound by §§5 and 6, with data access restricted and walled off from any linen-operations business;
   - Trutour gives advance notice of at least 30–60 days before the assignment; and
   - Vougeir has a right to terminate without penalty, with a full refund of prepaid fees, free transition assistance under §13.5, and data return under §5.5, if it objects to an assignee.
3. Make Change of Control parallel. Trutour's own Change of Control should be treated the same way, as draft v2 §14.2 did.

---

### Issue 4: Service-credit disputes go to New York law and forum; all else stays in Delaware (MEDIUM)

**Where:**
- Quality Agreement §9.1.
- License Agreement §1.3 (with §18.1).

**What the documents say:**
- **License Agreement §18.1.** Delaware law and exclusive jurisdiction of the courts in Wilmington, Delaware. Term Sheet §12.4 contemplated Delaware law and forum throughout.
- **Quality Agreement §9.1.** The Quality Agreement "and all disputes arising out of or relating to it, **including claims for Service Credits**, are governed by the **laws of the State of New York**." It gives exclusive jurisdiction to the courts "**located in New York County**, New York."
- **License Agreement §1.3.** The License Agreement prevails over the Quality Agreement, "except that the Quality Agreement controls on all matters relating to Service Levels and Service Credits, **including the resolution of disputes regarding them**."
  - Draft v2 §1.3 did *not* include the dispute-resolution language. It was added in the final version.

**Why it matters to Vougeir:**
- Because of §1.3, the New York clause governs Vougeir's uptime, service-level and Service Credit claims rather than being overridden by §18.1.
- A single serious outage would split across two laws and two *exclusive* forums:
  - Service Credits, plus the chronic-failure termination right under QA §7, would go to New York County.
  - Warranty (§8.2), data security (§5), damages and other claims would go to Wilmington.
- That creates a risk of duplicative litigation, inconsistent results, and arguments that one forum lacks jurisdiction over the other set of claims.
- It also invites Trutour to argue that Service Credits are the exclusive remedy for an outage in one forum while defending the damages claim in the other.
- The side letter (§4.3) applies §18 (Delaware) to itself but says the Quality Agreement applies to the new plants (§1.3). That extends the split to the Bethlehem and Cherry Hill plants.

**Recommended fix:**
1. Amend Quality Agreement §9.1 to adopt Delaware law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Wilmington, Delaware courts, consistent with License Agreement §18.1 and Term Sheet §12.4.
2. Also amend License Agreement §1.3 to delete "including the resolution of disputes regarding them." Provide expressly that §18.1 governs all disputes under both agreements. The QA §9.2 escalation procedure can be preserved as a pre-suit step.
3. Include both changes in the same amendment as Issues 1–3.

---

## 3. Documents Reviewed With No Separate Issue

- **Draft v2 (February 11, 2025).** This is a superseded, unsigned draft marked "Not for signature." It has no operative effect. It is useful as negotiating evidence because it shows that Trutour previously accepted the following positions, all of which changed in the signed version:
  - mutual assignment consent (§14.1);
  - a mutual Change of Control provision without "sole discretion" (§14.2);
  - no deemed-acceptance mechanism in §4.4; and
  - a §1.3 that did not route dispute resolution to the Quality Agreement.
- **Go-live confirmation email (May 19, 2025).** This confirms go-live at all five original Licensed Plants between May 5 and May 19, 2025 under §3.2, and the start of Service Levels under QA §2.1. No issue arises. The client should confirm that the $45,000 go-live milestone invoice has been paid or properly disputed.

---

## 4. Recommended Next Steps

1. **This week:** Confirm with the client the facts on the fee notice (delivery date, any earlier objection) and the merger agreement's consent and closing-condition treatment of the Trutour contract.
2. **Before closing (January 2027):** Send Trutour a consent request and proposed amendment covering:
   - Change of Control consent and revisions to §14.3 and §13.4 (Issue 1);
   - waiver of the §4.4 deadline, or an agreed fee for the contract year beginning March 1, 2027 (Issue 2);
   - mutual assignment restrictions with competitor and data protections (Issue 3); and
   - single Delaware law and forum across both agreements (Issue 4).
3. **Client advice:** Do not close the Ostrander transaction without Trutour's signed written consent, and diarize all §4.4 and §12.2 notice windows going forward.

Please let me know if you would like me to prepare the consent request and draft amendment.

**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 20, 2026
**Re:** Vougeir Linen Services, Inc. / Trutour Systems, LLC: Review of TruRoute Linen Suite License Documents

---

## 1. Background

Vougeir Linen Services, Inc. licenses the **TruRoute Linen Suite** from Trutour Systems, LLC. TruRoute is a hosted **RFID linen tracking and route management platform**. The license is under a Software License Agreement with an **Effective Date of March 1, 2025** (the "License Agreement"). Key terms:

- **Initial Term:** three years from the Effective Date (§12.1), then automatic one-year renewals (§12.2).
- **Annual License Fee:** $486,000 (§4.1).
- **Governing law and forum:** Delaware law, with exclusive jurisdiction in the state or federal courts in Wilmington (§18.1).

A companion Quality Agreement of the same date sets the Service Levels and Service Credits.

I reviewed all seven documents in the folder:

1. the License Agreement;
2. the Quality Agreement;
3. the January 17, 2025 term sheet;
4. Vougeir's September 14, 2026 fee objection letter;
5. Trutour's October 6, 2026 side letter adding the Bethlehem and Cherry Hill plants and increasing seats from 150 to 210;
6. the February 11, 2025 draft v2 of the license; and
7. Trutour's May 19, 2025 go-live confirmation email.

Draft v2 and the go-live email do not create issues of their own. Draft v2 is useful background, because it shows how several provisions moved against Vougeir between draft and signature.

The issues are listed below in order of priority.

---

## 2. Issues (Prioritized)

### Issue 1: Fee-increase objection was sent late, so the increase may be "deemed accepted"
**Priority: HIGH (time-sensitive)**

**Where:**
- License Agreement §4.4 (Fee Adjustments).
- Vougeir's letter to Trutour dated September 14, 2026, ¶1.

**What the documents show:**
- Section 4.4 lets Trutour raise the Annual License Fee effective on an anniversary of the Effective Date.
- Vougeir may object "within thirty (30) days after the date of Licensor's fee adjustment notice." If it does not, "the adjusted fee is deemed accepted by Licensee."
- Trutour's notice is dated **August 3, 2026**. It raises the fee from $486,000 to **$559,000** (about 15%), effective **March 1, 2027**.
- The notice satisfies the 90-day advance-notice requirement, because it was given about seven months before the anniversary.
- Counting from August 3, the objection window closed on **September 2, 2026**.
- Vougeir's objection letter is dated **September 14, 2026**, which is **12 days late**.
- The letter states that Vougeir "do[es] not accept the proposed increase" and expects continued invoicing at $486,000. On the contract terms, that position is likely unsupportable.

**Why it matters:**
- Trutour can treat the $559,000 fee as deemed accepted from March 1, 2027. That is a $73,000 increase per contract year.
- Under §4.4, the fallback to the existing fee applies only if Vougeir "objects within that period." Vougeir therefore loses the protection that would otherwise keep the fee at $486,000 if negotiations fail.
- The increase also flows through to the Monthly Fee used to calculate Service Credits under Quality Agreement §1.1(d). That effect is minor but should be noted.
- Draft v2 §4.4 did not contain the deemed-acceptance language. It was added in the executed version.
- Nothing in the folder shows that Vougeir has paid or otherwise agreed to the higher fee. Its position is weak, but it is not yet foreclosed.

**Recommended fix:**
- Before March 1, 2027, promptly seek a **written waiver** from Trutour of the timing defect, or a **negotiated fee resolution** documented as an amendment signed under §18.3.
- Useful leverage includes:
  - the new plant and seat fees under the side letter (about $76,000 per year for the plants plus $81,000 per year for the seats);
  - Trutour's interest in the relationship as it expands; and
  - the request in the letter for pricing justification.
- Do not rely on the September 14 letter as a valid §4.4 objection.
- Avoid conduct that could be read as acceptance, such as paying a $559,000 invoice without a reservation of rights.
- Going forward, docket all §4.4 notice dates. Consider proposing that the deemed-acceptance mechanic be removed, or that the window be extended, for example to 60 days.

---

### Issue 2: Trutour may assign the license to anyone, including a Vougeir competitor, without consent
**Priority: HIGH**

**Where:**
- License Agreement §14.1, compared with §14.2.
- Term sheet §11.1.

**What the documents show:**
- Section 14.1 permits Trutour to assign the Agreement "in whole or in part, to any Affiliate or to any third party without Licensee's consent." Trutour need only give notice within 30 days *after* the assignment takes effect.
- Under §14.2, by contrast, Vougeir cannot assign without Trutour's prior written consent.
- Term sheet §11.1 recorded a **mutual** restriction: "Neither party may assign without the other party's prior written consent."
- Draft v2 §14.1 also reflected a mutual consent requirement. The executed agreement departs from both.

**Why it matters:**
- The platform is hosted. It holds Vougeir's most commercially sensitive information: customer lists, delivery routes, pricing and linen-volume data (§1.1(e) "Licensee Data").
- Trutour could transfer the contract, and with it custody of that data, to a competing laundry or linen-rental operator or one of its affiliates.
- Vougeir would learn of the transfer only after the fact. It would have no right to object and no termination right.
- The confidentiality and data-use protections in §§5–6 would technically bind a permitted assignee under §14.4. However, Vougeir would depend on a competitor's compliance, with no prior vetting.
- "In whole or in part" also permits a split assignment. That could separate hosting and support from the counterparty responsible for performance.

**Recommended fix:** Amend §14.1 to restore the term-sheet position, that is, **Vougeir's prior written consent** for any assignment by Trutour. Fallback positions, in order:

1. Allow consent-free assignment only to an Affiliate, or to a successor to all or substantially all of Trutour's business, that is **not a competitor** of Vougeir. Define "competitor" by reference to commercial laundry and linen-rental services.
2. Require **advance** written notice of at least 30 days.
3. Require the assignee to assume all obligations in writing, including §§5–6 and the Quality Agreement.
4. Give Vougeir a **termination right** on any assignment to a competitor or without consent. On exercise, Vougeir would receive a pro rata refund, data return under §5.5, and transition assistance at no charge.
5. Prohibit partial assignments.

---

### Issue 3: Service-credit and outage disputes are split between New York and Delaware law and forums
**Priority: MEDIUM**

**Where:**
- Quality Agreement §9.1.
- License Agreement §1.3 (Order of Precedence) and §18.1.

**What the documents show:**
- License Agreement §18.1 selects **Delaware** law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Wilmington, Delaware courts. This is consistent with term sheet §12.4.
- Quality Agreement §9.1 provides that the Quality Agreement "and all disputes arising out of or relating to it, including claims for Service Credits," are governed by the **laws of the State of New York**. It also gives exclusive jurisdiction to the **courts located in New York County**.
- License Agreement §1.3 makes the Quality Agreement control "on all matters relating to Service Levels and Service Credits, **including the resolution of disputes regarding them**."
- The phrase in bold does not appear in draft v2 §1.3. It was added to the executed version.

**Why it matters:**
- Section 1.3 lets the New York clause override Delaware for service-level and service-credit claims. Everything else stays in Delaware.
- A single serious outage would split Vougeir's claims across two governing laws and two *exclusive* forums. For example:
  - Service Credits and chronic-failure termination under Quality Agreement §7 would go to New York.
  - Warranty breach (§8.2), data-security breach (§5) and damages claims, including uncapped claims under §10.3, would go to Delaware.
- That split raises cost and creates a risk of inconsistent results. It also invites forum fights over which claims belong where.
- Trutour could use the exclusive New York forum to delay or fragment Vougeir's claims.

**Recommended fix:**
- Conform both documents to a **single governing law and forum (Delaware / Wilmington)**:
  - amend Quality Agreement §9.1 to adopt License Agreement §18.1; and
  - delete "including the resolution of disputes regarding them" from License Agreement §1.3, so that precedence covers substantive service terms only.
- Keep the Quality Agreement §9.2 escalation procedure. Clarify that it does not toll or bar related claims under the License Agreement.
- This can be packaged with the Issue 1 and Issue 2 amendments.

---

## 3. Other Observations (Lower Priority)

- **Side letter (October 6, 2026):** It adds the Bethlehem, PA and Cherry Hill, NJ plants and 60 seats. Fees are $38,000 per plant per year, $1,350 per seat per year, and $12,500 implementation per plant, with a target go-live of February 15, 2027. It incorporates §§16 and 18 of the License Agreement. It does not address the Quality Agreement governing-law clause, so Issue 3 will also apply to the new plants. Confirm the countersigned version is in the file.
- **Go-live email (May 19, 2025):** It confirms go-live at all five original plants between May 5 and May 19, 2025, and that Service Levels apply from those dates. No issue identified. It may be useful evidence of performance baselines in any later service-credit dispute.
- **Draft v2:** It is not operative, but it shows that the mutual assignment clause, the narrower §1.3 precedence clause, and the absence of deemed acceptance in §4.4 were all changed against Vougeir before signing. This history supports asking Trutour to restore the negotiated positions.

---

## 4. Recommended Next Steps

1. **Immediately:** Open discussions with Trutour on the fee increase (Issue 1) and seek a written waiver or an agreed fee before March 1, 2027.
2. **In the same negotiation:** Propose a short amendment covering the assignment restrictions (Issue 2) and governing-law conformity (Issue 3).
3. Confirm the client's payment practices pending resolution, and add a reservation of rights to any payment at the increased rate.
4. Docket the key dates:
   - March 1, 2027 (fee anniversary);
   - February 15, 2027 (target go-live for the new plants);
   - December 1, 2027 (last day for a non-renewal notice before the Initial Term ends on March 1, 2028).

Please let me know if you would like me to prepare the waiver request and a draft amendment.
